newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor Secretary calls for renewed UPS talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor Secretary calls for renewed UPS talks.

text.p: U.S. Labour Secretary Alexis Herman urged United Parcel Service management and the Teamsters union to resume talks to avert a strike set for midnight EDT on Sunday (0400 GMT).
"UPS and Teamsters representatives should press on and not rest until they find the common ground that resolves this dispute with the least disruption," Herman said in a statement.
"I urge both parties to return to the bargaining table and negotiate in good faith until they reach a fair settlement," she said.
Teamsters union President Ron Carey left the talks at around 10 p.m. EDT (0200 GMT), saying a deal could not be reached and calling a midnight strike.
White House spokesman Barry Toiv said President Bill Clinton did not plan to use his authority under federal law to intervene.
"At this time, the administration does not believe that the standard for intervention under the Taft-Hartley Act has been met," Toiv said.
